solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Feature of garden city after call to incorporate river (8)

indicatorNotes.to incorporate: to incorporate is to take something into your body, so the call swallows the river letter

blocks.note: a bid is a call, as in bridge

annotation.surface: A garden city whose plan includes a river running through it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Garden city' reads as one phrase, the planned town; split it, and 'garden' belongs to the definition while 'city' is BATH.
annotation.definitionFit: A birdbath is a basin set out as an ornament in a garden.

entries.clue: Shepherdess’s dance involving physical exercise and energy (2,4)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is literally to roll up inside, so the dance wraps round the exercise and energy

blocks.note: PE = physical exercise, the school lesson

annotation.surface: A shepherdess performing a vigorous, energetic dance.
annotation.walkthrough: Little Bo Peep is the nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep. The 's stands for 'has', linking the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Bo Peep is the best-known shepherdess of nursery rhyme.

entries.clue: Pathway unconventional, but getting right to the top (5)

indicatorNotes.getting right to the top: the R (right) moves up to the first position

blocks.note: R = right, moved from the end of OUTRE to the front

annotation.surface: An unconventional career path that nonetheless reaches the top.
annotation.walkthrough: Nothing is added or lost: the R already in OUTRE simply travels to the top of this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A route is a way or path from one place to another.

entries.clue: Internet commentator and forestry worker supporting book (7)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down entry, LOGGER sits under B

annotation.surface: Two people, an online pundit and a lumberjack, lined up behind a book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' works only because this is a down clue: the supporter is underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a blogger posts opinion pieces online, which is commentary published on the internet.

entries.clue: The strike will incur a lot of staggering urgent government business (5-4,4)

indicatorNotes.will incur: to incur is to bring something on yourself, so THE takes on the staggering inside it
indicatorNotes.a lot of: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so REELING loses its last letter

blocks.note: used as it stands, split open
REELING = staggering, cut short to REELIN and put inside THE

annotation.surface: A strike that will cause a great deal of alarming disruption to government work.
annotation.walkthrough: A three-line whip is the UK Parliament's strictest instruction to MPs to attend and vote, underlined three times on the party's notice. 'The strike' look like one noun phrase, a walkout; they are two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A three-line whip marks a vote as urgent business for the government's own members.

entries.clue: Diplomat’s gift starts off incredibly cunning ruse (6)

indicatorNotes.starts off: the starting letters of the next two words

blocks.note: tact is the talent a diplomat needs

annotation.surface: A diplomat's present launches an unbelievably sly scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gift' pretends to be a present handed over; here it is a talent.
annotation.definitionFit: A tactic is a scheme or manoeuvre, much like a ruse.

entries.clue: A curtailed court case involving America and another country (7)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: TRIAL loses its tail, the last letter
indicatorNotes.involving: a case involving someone has them caught up in it, so the shortened trial surrounds the country

annotation.surface: A shortened legal case between the United States and some other nation.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition says 'another' country because America is already in the clue as the first one.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Austria is one of many countries, and 'another' separates it from the America already in the wordplay.

entries.clue: We will capture circuit and end of race using special photography (4-5)

annotation.definitionNote: TIME-LAPSE is an adjective, so the definition is the whole phrase 'using special photography'

indicatorNotes.will capture: to capture is to take prisoner and hold, so TIMES holds the circuit inside it
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a lap is one circuit of a track, placed inside TIMES

annotation.surface: A newspaper team plan to photograph a lap and the finish of a race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'We' is the setter speaking for the paper, so it gives TIMES; the lap and the race also make it sound like sports reporting.
annotation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography takes frames at long intervals so slow change looks fast.

entries.clue: Mediterranean islander represented in Troy epic (8)

indicatorNotes.represented in: TROY EPIC re-presented as a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A man from a Mediterranean island appearing in the Iliad.
annotation.walkthrough: The Trojan War setting keeps the reader in ancient Greece, near enough to Cyprus to make the answer feel at home in the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A Cypriote (or Cypriot) is someone from Cyprus, an island in the eastern Mediterranean.

entries.clue: Cartoon dog and cat keeping animator ultimately a rich person (9)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold on to it, so CAT holds the letter inside
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the final letter

blocks.note: last letter of animatoR, inside CAT

annotation.surface: Cartoon characters holding on to the animator who made his fortune from them.
annotation.walkthrough: The cartoon surface makes 'a rich person' look like Walt Disney himself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone whose power comes from wealth.

entries.clue: Potent starlet revealed by my working? (6,7)

annotation.definition: Potent starlet revealed by my working?

indicatorNotes.working: the letters of POTENT STARLET put to work in a new order

annotation.surface: A scout boasting that a promising young actress was discovered through their own efforts.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the answer: a talent spotter's work is revealing promising starlets, and rearranging the words 'potent starlet' reveals the talent spotter.
annotation.definitionFit: A talent spotter finds promising performers, such as a potent starlet.

entries.clue: A lot of sentimental nonsense reflected by completed review (3,2)

indicatorNotes.A lot of: most of MUSH: the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.reflected: MUS read back to front, as in a mirror

blocks.note: MUSH = sentimental nonsense, cut to MUS and then reversed

annotation.surface: A finished review calls something mostly soppy drivel.
annotation.walkthrough: UP for completed is as in 'your time is up'. 'Review' is a verb here: to sum up is to review the main points.
annotation.definitionFit: To sum up is to review or recapitulate the main points.

entries.clue: English Republican backed following European stand (7)

indicatorNotes.backed: the three pieces read back to front
indicatorNotes.following: E comes after ENG and REP

annotation.surface: An English Republican who has retreated behind a European position.
annotation.walkthrough: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, a branched stand holding fruit or flowers. 'Backed' reverses the whole string ENG REP E, not just the Republican.
annotation.definitionFit: An epergne is a decorative table stand with branches for dishes.

entries.clue: Body of learning that is recalled about large element of Rhine mythology (7)

indicatorNotes.recalled: IE called back, read in reverse
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so LORE and the reversed EI sit either side of the large letter

blocks.note: lore = a body of traditional knowledge
IE = id est, that is, reversed
L = large, the clothing size; it goes between LORE and EI

annotation.surface: A scholarly tradition remembered around a major strand of Rhineland legend.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine where, in legend, a siren lured boatmen to their deaths.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lorelei siren is a figure of Rhine legend.

entries.clue: Released Iran papers etc in coverage from that area? (7,6)

indicatorNotes.Released: the letters are set free to rearrange

annotation.surface: Leaked Iranian documents getting press coverage from that region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' looks like news reporting of the released papers; it is floor coverage, and 'that area' is Iran, once Persia.
annotation.definitionFit: A Persian carpet is a floor covering from Iran.

entries.clue: Isn’t in lead over the whole war game (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so the contraction sits within the chemical symbol
indicatorNotes.over: over means above, and in a down entry the first part sits above ALL

blocks.note: Pb, the chemical symbol for lead

annotation.surface: Someone denying they are in charge of the entire war game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' wants to mean 'in charge'; it is the metal, whose symbol PB comes from Latin plumbum.
annotation.definitionFit: Paintball is a mock combat game fought with paint-pellet guns.

entries.clue: English dog, surrounded by offspring, reared to be smart (6,2)

annotation.definitionNote: SPRUCE UP is a verb meaning make smart; 'to be smart' gives the result of it

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: PUPS goes round E and CUR
indicatorNotes.reared: in a down entry, the whole is raised up, read bottom to top

blocks.note: a dog's offspring are pups, split open
a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: An English dog among its own litter, brought up to be well-groomed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reared' sounds like raising a family; in a down clue it turns the whole string upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: sprucing up a room or yourself leaves it neat and well turned out, which is what smart means in British use.

entries.clue: Bit of childish fun agitating press barons, I finally assume (9,4)

blocks.note: last letter of assumE, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone guessing that stirring up newspaper tycoons is a bit of childish mischief.
annotation.walkthrough: Prisoners' base is an old children's chasing game in which each team tries to catch and hold players from the other side.
annotation.definitionFit: Prisoners' base is a traditional playground game, fun for children.

entries.clue: Lavish work curtailed, then advanced (7)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: OPUS loses its tail, the last letter
indicatorNotes.then: then means next in sequence, so the loan word comes after the shortened work

blocks.note: to advance money is to lend it

annotation.surface: A grand project cut short, then pushed forward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' reads as moved forward; it is money advanced, a loan.
annotation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavish, richly luxurious.

entries.clue: Depression, drowned in beer, not yielding much? (2,5)

indicatorNotes.drowned in: something drowned in a drink is submerged inside it, so the depression goes inside the beer

blocks.note: a dent is a depression in a surface

annotation.surface: Someone depressed, drinking beer, and getting little out of life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' and 'drowned in beer' paint a sad drinker; 'not yielding much' sounds like poor returns but means firm to the bite, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Pasta cooked al dente is firm, giving only a little when bitten.

entries.clue: Likely to have Liberals displaced in Yorkshire town (6)

indicatorNotes.displaced: the Ls change places within the word

blocks.note: the two Ls (Liberals) are the letters moved

annotation.surface: A Yorkshire town probably going to see its Liberal councillors removed.
annotation.walkthrough: Ilkley is a spa town in West Yorkshire, known for Ilkley Moor. Moving the two Ls of LIKELY is all it takes.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Ilkley is one particular town in West Yorkshire, famous from the song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at'.

entries.clue: Gamble, losing power? Regret past fabrication (7)

indicatorNotes.losing: to lose something is to be left without it, so the gamble word drops a letter

blocks.note: to punt is to place a bet
P = power, the letter removed from PUNT to leave UNT
ruth is an old word for regret or pity; 'past' marks it as archaic

annotation.surface: A gambler, out of luck, regretting something made up in the past.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Past' does not mean earlier events: it flags RUTH as an old-fashioned word, the root of 'ruthless'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fabrication is a made-up story, a polite word for a lie.

entries.clue: Old ideal shattered, split by pressure of some Freudian concept (7)

indicatorNotes.shattered: IDEAL broken into a new order
indicatorNotes.split by: EDIAL is broken open by P

annotation.surface: A long-held ideal falling apart under the strain of psychoanalysis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' makes the definition adjectival to match OEDIPAL, relating to Freud's Oedipus complex.
annotation.definitionFit: Oedipal relates to the Oedipus complex, one of Freud's central ideas.

entries.clue: Chief, though not number one? (5)

blocks.note: chief as an adjective: main, principal, first in rank
a kind of whole number; by mathematical convention 1 is excluded from this class

annotation.surface: A leader who is somehow not the top person.
annotation.walkthrough: Chief sounds like number one, so the clue seems to contradict itself; but in maths 1 is excluded from the primes.
annotation.definitionFit: Prime means chief or principal, and a prime is a number that cannot be 1.

entries.clue: Delete time stamp except at the outset (5)

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
first letters of Stamp and Except

annotation.surface: An instruction to remove a time stamp, apart from the one at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time stamp' reads as one computing term, and 'except' as a word of exclusion; both are split, and 'except' simply supplies its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to wipe out text or data, and the time stamp surface puts it in computer terms.

entries.clue: Unused capacity? Way best to harness it when recalled (9)

indicatorNotes.to harness: a harness straps round a horse, so the way is strapped round the 'it'
indicatorNotes.when recalled: recalled means called back, so the whole string is read in reverse

blocks.note: a lane is a way, split open

annotation.surface: A question about spare capacity, and advice on the best way to make use of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads naturally in order, but the answer comes out only after LAITNE and TOP are joined and then turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Potential is capacity not yet put to use.

entries.clue: The very thing to be included in college constitution (6)

indicatorNotes.to be included in: something included in a group is enclosed by it, so the very thing goes within the college

blocks.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a British college, split open

annotation.surface: Just the right item for a college's constitution.
annotation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a British higher-education college, mostly renamed as universities in 1992.
annotation.definitionFit: A polity is a form of government or civil constitution.

entries.clue: Trees etc depicted in lines by English writer (8)

indicatorNotes.by: by means next to, as in 'sit by me', so the lines sit alongside the writer

blocks.note: RY = railway, a set of lines

annotation.surface: Trees and plants described in verse by an English poet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests lines of verse; it is railway lines.
annotation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage such as trees and plants.
